outcome: Pregnancy complications (miscarriages, pre-eclampsia, fetal growth restriction, gestational diabetes)
cohort: A total of 14 pregnant patients (9 VNS, 3 DBS, 2 RNS) experiencing 22 pregnancies, who were treated with neuromodulation for focal epilepsy, generalized epilepsy, or Tourette syndrome.
finding: The study suggests that implanted neuromodulation devices (VNS, DBS, RNS) do not seem to pose a risk of neuromodulation-related teratogenicity during pregnancy.
mod_finding: Eight of the 22 pregnancies (5 VNS, 1 DBS, 2 RNS) resulted in delivery by cesarean section.
